## Required Library
```r
# summary() is in base R, loaded by default — no package installation needed
```

## Syntax

```{r, eval=FALSE}
summary(object, ...)
```
::: {.desc-item}
`summary(object)` returns a compact summary of an object.
Because `summary()` is generic, output depends on the class of the object.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Why does summary() look different each time?
`summary()` dispatches different methods based on object type.

- Numeric vector: min, quartiles, median, mean, max
- Data frame: summary for each column
- Linear model (`lm`): residuals, coefficients, residual standard error, R-squared, F-statistic
:::

## Examples

<div class="example-section">
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Summarize a numeric vector</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
x <- c(98.4, 99.1, 100.3, 101.0, 99.8, 100.2)

summary(x)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Summarize each column in a data frame</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

calibration <- tibble(
  conc_ug_ml = c(0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0),
  absorbance = c(0.003, 0.057, 0.110, 0.226, 0.441, 0.889)
)

summary(calibration)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Summarize an lm() model and extract R-squared</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

calibration <- tibble(
  conc_ug_ml = c(0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0),
  absorbance = c(0.003, 0.057, 0.110, 0.226, 0.441, 0.889)
)

model <- lm(absorbance ~ conc_ug_ml, data = calibration)
model_summary <- summary(model)

model_summary

r2 <- model_summary$r.squared
cat("R-squared:", signif(r2, 4), "\n")
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Compare summary() and coef() for a model</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

calibration <- tibble(
  conc_ug_ml = c(0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0),
  absorbance = c(0.003, 0.057, 0.110, 0.226, 0.441, 0.889)
)

model <- lm(absorbance ~ conc_ug_ml, data = calibration)

cat("coef(model):\n")
print(coef(model))

cat("\nsummary(model)$coefficients:\n")
print(summary(model)$coefficients)
```
</div>
</details>

</div>

## Argument Overview
<p class="arg-intro">Required arguments must be included when using a function while optional arguments can be included on demand.</p>

::: {.arg-section}
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>object</code> — object to summarize <span class="arg-types">any R object</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
The object for which summary information should be produced.

```r
summary(x)
summary(df)
summary(model)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> numeric, factor, data frame, model object, and many others</p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>...</code> — method-specific options <span class="arg-types">various</span> <span class="arg-badge optional">Optional</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Additional arguments passed to class-specific summary methods.
Most common beginner use is simply `summary(object)` with no extra arguments.

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> depends on object class</p>
</div>
</details>
:::
